title: Analysis of sugars and amino acids in aphid honeydew by hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography – Mass spectrometry
author: Nguyen, Owens, et al.

steps.title: Prepare individual analyte stock solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve approximately 25 mg of each sugar or amino acid into 25 mL methanol/water (10/90, v/v) to make ~1000 mg L⁻¹ stock solutions (weigh with a Mettler XS64 balance).

steps.title: Prepare working stock solutions
steps.instruction: Combine the individual stocks to make two 25 mL working solutions in methanol/water (10/90, v/v): one containing all sugars at 50 mg L⁻¹ and one containing all amino acids at 50 mg L⁻¹.

steps.title: Create calibration standards
steps.instruction: From each working solution prepare five 1‑mL calibration standards at 10, 5, 2.5, 1 and 0.5 mg L⁻¹ in methanol/water (10/90, v/v). Serially dilute the 5 mg L⁻¹ standard to obtain additional 0.25, 0.10 and 0.05 mg L⁻¹ standards (also 1 mL each). Store all standards at 4 °C until analysis.

steps.title: Prepare MS optimization standards
steps.instruction: Make ~1 mg L⁻¹ sugar and amino‑acid standards by adding 1 µL of the ~1000 mg L⁻¹ stock to 1 mL methanol/water (10/90, v/v).

steps.title: Prepare sugar LC/MS mobile phases
steps.instruction: Make mobile phase A: acetonitrile/water (30/70, v/v) with 0.10 % (v/v) ammonium hydroxide; mobile phase B: acetonitrile/water (80/20, v/v) with 0.10 % (v/v) ammonium hydroxide.

steps.title: Set sugar gradient and run conditions
steps.instruction: Program the gradient: 0 min 100 % B, ramp to 50 % B at 8 min, return to 100 % B at 8.2 min, then re‑equilibrate for 10.8 min before the next injection. Use a flow rate of 0.6000 mL min⁻¹, column temperature 35 °C, injection volume 4 µL, and a total run time of 20 min.

steps.title: Prepare amino‑acid LC/MS mobile phases
steps.instruction: Make mobile phase A: water with 0.15 % (v/v) formic acid and 10 mM ammonium formate; mobile phase B: acetonitrile with 0.15 % (v/v) formic acid.

steps.title: Set amino‑acid gradient and run conditions
steps.instruction: Program the gradient: 0 min 85 % B, ramp to 80 % B at 6 min, 70 % B at 10 min, return to 100 % B at 10.3 min, then re‑equilibrate for 8.7 min. Use a flow rate of 0.6000 mL min⁻¹, column temperature 35 °C, injection volume 4 µL, and a total run time of 20 min.

steps.title: Extract honeydew from field samples
steps.instruction: Collect honeydew on foil squares surrounding aphid‑colonized inflorescences for 24 h. After measuring droplet density, place a subsample of each foil into a 50 mL polypropylene centrifuge tube, add 2 mL 18 MΩ DI water pre‑heated to 80 °C (Thermo Scientific air‑displacement pipette), sonicate for 15 min at 60 °C (FS20D sonicator, Fisher Scientific), then transfer 1 mL of the extract to a Waters autosampler vial for direct LC/MS or LC/MS/MS analysis.

steps.title: Dilute high‑concentration extracts
steps.instruction: For samples exceeding the calibration range, dilute 1:20 or 1:400 with methanol/water (10/90, v/v). For 1:20, add 50 µL original extract to a new autosampler vial and add 950 µL methanol/water using a Hamilton gastight syringe; vortex 10 s. For 1:400, take 50 µL of the 1:20 dilution and add 950 µL methanol/water (10/90, v/v).

steps.title: Concentrate low‑concentration extracts
steps.instruction: For extracts below the LOQ (amino acids), transfer 500 µL of the original aqueous extract to a Waters autosampler vial (air‑displacement pipette), evaporate in a chemical fume hood at 25 °C for one week, re‑suspend the residue in 50 µL 18 MΩ organic‑free water, cap and sonicate in a 25 °C water bath for 15 min (degas mode), then transfer the 50 µL to a 100 µL PolySpring insert before LC/MS analysis.
